messages:
ariane (DevEx): Quick heads-up — proposing that next SDK release enables client-side routing by default (python/ts/go). Want platform + infra input on telemetry/quota impacts before we flip it.

sam (Platform): Why default to client-side? Server routing gives us centralized quota accounting and fallback behaviour.

ariane (DevEx): Primary reason is UX: apps get lower-latency path selection (local hints) and can prefer cheaper variants. Customers have asked for client-level control. We can make it opt-out.

mike (SDK): Important: if SDK emits full routing headers (model selection + policy) we could double-count or confuse quota shards. Proposal: SDK should only emit a lightweight route_hint header, e.g.:

    X-Redwood-Route-Hint: model=redwood-fast;policy=client

That keeps final decision server-side for billing/audit but lets runtime optimize.

sam (Platform): That sounds better. But we need a mapping in telemetry so console dashboards show the hint vs actual served model. Otherwise graphs will be misleading.

grace (Product): Console UX: we want to let customers filter by "client requested model" vs "actual served model" for rollout analysis. Can we standardize keys?

ryan (Eng-Infra): We also need to avoid leaking experiment metadata in telemetry. If route_hint contains A/B variant names we should sanitize or hash them before sending to analytics.

mike (SDK): Agreed. Implementation detail: SDK exposes env/config flag REDWOOD_SDK_ROUTING=auto|client|server; default will be "auto" which emits only route_hint unless explicit server mode is set. Sample config: 

    // js
    new RedwoodClient({ routing: process.env.REDWOOD_SDK_ROUTING || 'auto' })

sam (Platform): Need to confirm billing impact. If gateway ignores route_hint and routes to fallback, billing should attribute to served model. Who de-dupes telemetry traces?

ryan (Eng-Infra): Gateway will be source-of-truth for billing. Telemetry pipeline: ingest will accept both hint and served_model fields; aggregation uses served_model for cost metrics, hint for UX metrics. We'll add a migration flag so dashboards can show both for 30 days.

ariane (DevEx): Break strategy for older SDKs: keep server-default unchanged for 2 releases, then switch default to 'auto' for new minor with a clear changelog + deprecation warnings in logs.

mike (SDK): We'll add a runtime warning when env is unset: "SDK routing default will change in X. Set REDWOOD_SDK_ROUTING to opt out." Also add tests in sdk-ci-bot to validate header shape.

sdk-ci-bot: CI: added unit tests to assert X-Redwood-Route-Hint format; failing on malformed tokens — pipeline green on branch.

grace (Product): Rollout UX request: Console should surface what percentage of requests had client_hints vs server-decisions and allow a canary slider (5/20/50/100%).

sam (Platform): Ops ask: please include a toggle in the control plane to force "server-only" per-customer in case of quota mismatch or regulatory reasons.

mike (SDK): We can include a per-customer override: server sends a control flag via account config; sdk polls and respects server_overrides.routing=server if present.

ryan (Eng-Infra): Action items: 1) infra to add served_model + hint fields to telemetry mapping and 30-day dual-views (owner: ryan). 2) platform to confirm billing uses served_model (owner: sam). 3) sdk teams to implement REDWOOD_SDK_ROUTING auto + runtime warning + hashing of variant names (owner: mike). 4) product to specify console filters and canary UI (owner: grace).

ariane (DevEx): timeline idea: announce change in SDK changelog & release notes next week, cut canary SDK release with default 'auto' to 5% of users via npm/pypi tagging, then full default flip in 2 weeks if no issues.

sam (Platform): Sounds reasonable. I'll review billing test cases by EOD.

mike (SDK): I'll open the SDK PRs today and add a short migration doc to devex docs.

ariane (DevEx): Perfect — I'll draft the changelog blurb and add a snippet for console screenshots. Thanks everyone :rocket:
